title: From Chat to Doing: How Modern AI Learns to Look Things Up
subtitle: Your saved NVIDIA courses point to one shift: AI that retrieves, acts, and runs anywhere.
intro: You saved 7 free NVIDIA courses that promise production-ready AI, not just chat. The secret isn't a bigger brain — it's giving AI tools to look things up and act.
takeaway: Modern AI wins by combining a language model with retrieval and specialized hardware, but only if you check what it found.

sections.heading: Analogy: the intern with a library card
sections.body: Think of an intern who sounds smart but forgets details. Give them tools and they become useful. In AI, the intern is a Large Language Model (LLM) — a text-prediction system. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is the library card to search your documents. An Agent is the phone to call tools. CUDA and Jetson Nano are the workshop to run AI fast.

sections.heading: Why does this exist?: answers that stay current
sections.body: Retraining an LLM is slow and expensive. RAG keeps knowledge outside the model instead. You ask -> it retrieves relevant docs -> the LLM answers using them. Example from your saves: a Video AI App can answer about your own videos without retraining. Edge AI on Jetson Nano — a tiny edge device — can do this on-device, not just in the cloud.

sections.heading: What can go wrong?: confident, wrong, and leaky
sections.body: A RAG Agent can still fail predictably. Bad retrieval means it finds the wrong document and hallucinates — sounds confident but is wrong. Stale or private data means outdated or leaked files cause bad answers. Hardware limits mean CUDA helps speed, but Jetson Nano has little memory — too much video at once crashes. Always check sources.

steps.narration: You ask a question that needs current, private knowledge.
RAG searches your documents for relevant passages.
The LLM drafts an answer grounded in what was retrieved.
A RAG Agent can then call tools or run video AI steps.
CUDA on GPUs or Jetson Nano at the edge makes it run fast enough to use.

quiz.q: What does RAG do for an LLM?
options: It lets the model search external documents before answering
It deletes the model's training data
It replaces the GPU with a CPU
quiz.why: RAG = Retrieval-Augmented Generation. It retrieves relevant docs first, so answers stay current without retraining.

quiz.q: What fails first if usage grows 100x on a Jetson Nano edge device?
options: The model becomes more accurate automatically
Memory and compute run out, causing crashes or slowdowns
quiz.why: Edge devices like Jetson Nano have limited memory and GPU power. Scaling video AI 100x overwhelms them first.

quiz.q: Why add digital fingerprinting to AI content?
options: To identify and protect AI-generated content
To remove the need for CUDA
quiz.why: Fingerprinting helps track provenance and security — knowing what was AI-made, as listed in your NVIDIA courses.

extra: NVIDIA Jetson Nano is a small edge AI computer often used for video AI demos with limited RAM.
